response.sql: SELECT f.orderslink, o.mktnote, AVG(f.rebrate) as avg_rebrate, SUM(f.rebtotal) as total_rebate FROM fees f INNER JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate >= 0.0009 GROUP BY f.orderslink, o.mktnote ORDER BY total_rebate DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: "0.0009 as the cutoff" means feerate >= 0.0009 (inclusive). High-rate fees are those at or above the cutoff threshold.

"Ignoring missing values" refers to standard SQL aggregate behavior: AVG() and SUM() inherently skip NULL values during calculation, rather than requiring explicit filtering of rows with NULL rebrate or rebtotal before aggregation.
In SQLite's native sort order, ORDER BY total_rebate DESC naturally places NULL values last, satisfying the "missing last" requirement without additional syntax.

alternatives.interpretation: If "high-rate" means strictly above the cutoff (not including the cutoff itself), use feerate > 0.0009
